segments.text: The Eiffel Tower is always the same height. Well, that's not exactly true. In summer, it gets taller.
The tower is made of iron, and iron expands when it heats up. On a hot day, the tower can grow by about {15 centimeters.|fifteen centimeters.}
Here's the wild part. The sun heats one side more than the other, so the top slowly leans away from the sun during the day.
In fact, the tower was never meant to stay. It was built for a World's Fair in {1889,|eighteen eighty nine,} with a permit for just twenty years.
It was saved by science. Its height made it the perfect radio antenna, so Paris decided to keep it.
That's not all. Every seven years or so, it gets repainted by hand, with about sixty tons of paint.
So the Eiffel Tower isn't always the same height. It breathes with the seasons.
